The catalog has NO per-campaign-type capability at all, so there is currently no way to express live-call versus IVR versus SMS. IVR (robocall, simple_ivr, complex_ivr) and SMS (message) campaigns are served by the SAME routes as live-call campaigns and differ only by campaign.type, so any denial has to be type-aware. Sidebar visibility is 100% hasMinRole; there is no capability check anywhere in the UI.
rootCause: Authorization was modelled as a role comparison from the start and every check since has followed that shape. The capability layer grew beside it rather than replacing it, and the catalog was never extended to express campaign-type distinctions, so capability-by-capability policy is enforced ad hoc in whichever component happened to check it.
resolution: The vocabulary is settled: #2030 reported on 2026-10-19 (docs/adr/0039-role-checks-become-capability-checks.md) and says to grow PRODUCT_CAPABILITIES in app/lib/capabilities.ts rather than invent a second model, and to leave workspace-customized permissions to a later decision. currentBehavior: Campaign membership is a relation, but it does not appear to confer the broader capability, and the broader capability does not appear to be scoped back down to the campaigns they are actually on.

recommendedTitle: Reconcile audio objects left unattached after campaign update failure
summary: Audio upload ownership and attachment reconciliation need a durable protocol before a safe cleanup implementation can ship.
currentBehavior: The audio action has no cleanup after an empty or failed campaign update. A thrown database error can leave commit status uncertain; immediate deletion can remove an attached object. Current source/test evidence does not establish physical orphan counts or crash recovery.
rootCause: Object upload and campaign attachment have separate acknowledgement/failure boundaries and no durable lifecycle record or reference/deletion coordination.
resolution: Validate an upload ownership and attachment reconciliation protocol using existing media/storage/job patterns, then split implementation tasks as needed. Retain uncertain results until authoritative reconciliation and prevent attachment/deletion races. #2355 can proceed independently.
existingTests: Actual-route audit proves storage-call ordering before an empty scoped update; provider/database I/O is stubbed.
missingTests: Durable state-transition, uncertain commit, duplicate retry, restart, reference-read failure and reference/deletion race controls with suitable DB/storage integration.
acceptanceCriteria: Define durable upload ownership and attachment state using existing media/storage and job patterns where they fit. Do not add a route-local garbage collector.
An upload that is known to be unattached can be reclaimed. A confirmed attachment is retained. An uncertain write result is retained until authoritative reconciliation resolves it.
The durable retry/reconciliation record survives a crash after upload or an uncertain database acknowledgement. Unresolved cases remain visible to operators and are retried.

Reconciliation cannot delete an existing or shared object. It verifies owned object identity and current attachment references; coordinate reference checks with supported attachment writes so a new attachment cannot race deletion.
Cleanup failures cannot replace the original user error or falsely report success. They retain actionable operator evidence and durable retry state.

Cover successful attachment, known rejection, uncertain commit, failed reference read, duplicate retries, process restart and a reference/deletion race with real state transitions and appropriate database/storage integration controls.
Verify deployed behavior and release promotion before closing the task. Do not claim physical orphan cleanup from mocked storage calls.
trackerRecommendation: Validate an upload ownership and attachment reconciliation protocol using existing media/storage/job patterns, then split implementation tasks as needed. Retain uncertain results until authoritative reconciliation and prevent attachment/deletion races. #2355 can proceed independently.

recommendedTitle: Dual-lockfile drift gate never compares the two lockfiles, so CI validates a dependency tree the production worker image does not install
summary: Split first. The drift guard validates Bun against package.json, while CI and production still resolve different provider SDK versions.
currentBehavior: Current source at dev@03c3e15a still runs only bun install --frozen-lockfile --dry-run. Fresh installs confirm Twilio 5.13.1 in npm and 5.4.4 in Bun. The full gate passes despite that difference. .bun-version is 1.2.15, Docker uses 1.3.5, and Dockerfile.worker still omits --frozen-lockfile.
rootCause: scripts/check-bun-lockfile.mjs implements the dual-lockfile drift gate as `bun install --frozen-lockfile --dry-run` (line 21), and that command compares bun.lock with package.json only: it never reads package-lock.json, even though the script's own header (lines 4-13) states the gate exists because 'Adding or changing a dependency with one package manager leaves the other lockfile stale' and that the failure surfaces 'inside the Railway image build', and its own line 12 claims it fails 'when the two lockfiles disagree'. The two lockfiles are resolved by two different resolvers - npm with `legacy-peer-deps=true` from .npmrc, which ignores peer dependencies, and bun with its own resolver,…
resolution: Split resolver-version/worker-freeze alignment, explicit peer/platform comparison rules, the comparison guard, and dependency-family alignment into atomic tasks. Preserve the current peer policy until its change has consumer proof. Do not put a global package upgrade into a targeted security patch.
existingTests: Fresh installed-consumer proofs confirm the live npm/Bun Twilio version difference; the current full CI passes because its Bun guard checks only manifest satisfaction.
The earlier audit measured broad version and package-set differences. Recompute the complete matrix after the targeted patches before defining a parity guard.
missingTests: A regression test for this behaviour fails on the current source and passes with the fix (kill-check: revert the fix and confirm the test goes red).
A negative control for the same path keeps passing, so the fix does not silently widen access.
acceptanceCriteria: The drift gate should assert that the dependency tree CI installs and tests (package-lock.json, via `npm ci`) is the same tree the production images install (bun.lock, via `bun install`), so that the artifact which passed install, typecheck, lint and test is the artifact that is deployed. Any divergence between the two resolved trees - including a newer version of a credential-handling dependency landing in only one of them, and a package present in one tree but absent from the other - should fail the build before the image is produced.
trackerRecommendation: 2026-10-28 source review changes the earlier S-sized Fix now verdict: this is a multi-step dependency and CI task. Keep #3071, #3072 and #3073 atomic and require their individual fresh-consumer proofs. General parity remains unresolved.
